findings.evidence: The paragraph states that R and V_theta are measurable and that 0 <= V_theta/(R vee 1) <= 1, then infers that the ratio is integrable. The cited expectation definition also requires the ratio to be measurable, and this step is unstated. Since R and V_theta take values in {0,...,m}, measurability follows by partitioning into the finitely many measurable cells {R=r, V_theta=v} and noting the ratio is constant on each cell; add that argument before concluding integrability.

Step 3.1 says the full-real threshold equivalences in steps 2.1 and 2.2 transfer rational-threshold sufficiency from condition 2 to conditions 3–5. Those equivalences do not establish the claim under rational-only hypotheses, and step 2.2 proves the reduction only for condition 2. Close the inference using density and sigma-algebra operations, for example {f >= a}=intersection_{q rational, q<a}{f >= q}, {f < a}=union_{q rational, q<a}{f < q}, and {f <= a}=intersection_{q rational, q>a}{f <= q}.
